In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
repeated ECS increases concentrations of NPY in the occipotal cortex and hippocampus, and that the NPY consists of intact NPY, sulphoxidated NPY and no short C‐ terminal homologues.

the ECS‐induced increase in NPY‐like immunoreactive material (NPY‐Ll) in the rat hippocampus and cortex is due to increased concentrations of intact NPY and sulphoxidated NPY, but not to increased concentrations of short NPY homologues.
the NPY‐like immunoreactive material (NPY‐Li) in the rat hippocampus and occipital cortex consists of NPY (1–36) and sulphoxide NPY.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the increased NPY concentrations in the occipial cortex and hippocampus after repeated ECS are not due to a molecular heterogeneity of NPY, but rather to an increased concentration of intact NPY and sulphoxidated forms.
NPY is not heterogeneous in the brain of rats subjected to repeated ECS.
the NPY in the rat brain is mainly intact NPY (36 amino acids) with only small amounts of C‐terminal homologue peptides, and no short N‐terminal fragments were detected.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown the presence of NPY‐like immunoreactive material in the rat brain that does not crossreact with the N‐terminal antiserum.
the NPY‐LI in rat brain is mainly composed of intact NPY and the sulphoxidized NPY and not short C‐terminal NPY homologues.

the NPY system is affected by ECS, which is in line with other reports showing that ECS affects other neurotransmitter/neuromodulator systems, e.g., the serotonergic, noradrenergic and dopaminergic systems.
